title: Redwood discovery - Sorento AI - latency & throughput
summary: Discovery focused on p95 latency targets and throughput for streaming inference. Sorento currently evaluates hosted vs dedicated vs private options; main constraints are p95 < 250ms for short chat prompts, 20k concurrent sessions, and ability to sustain 50k tokens/sec aggregate with streaming. Next steps: run focused token/sec benchmark, share security pack, propose Dedicated sizing and pilot plan.
action_items: Alex Chen: Send Dedicated pricing + sizing spreadsheet (due: 2026-03-09)
Priya Kapoor: Share benchmark harness and sample workloads, request access to a small test dataset (due: 2026-03-08)
James Park: Provide representative traffic profile and sample prompts (due: 2026-03-07)
next_steps: Run token/sec and p95 streaming benchmark in Redwood hosted sandbox
Share SOC2 + encryption/KMS docs and SSO details
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-05 15:30 UTC
Duration: 42m
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Maria Lopez (Sorento Head of ML), James Park (Platform Eng), Ellen Wu (CTO)

Summary (auto): short call to nail down latency/throughput targets, decide whether Hosted can meet needs or Dedicated/Private needed. Discuss security/compliance and next steps for POC.

[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Alex from Redwood, with Priya our systems SE. how's everyone doing?
[00:07] Maria Lopez: Good, thanks. we wanted to focus today on latency and throughput. we're running a customer-facing chat product, and p95 is our SL0 for interactive queries.
[00:14] Priya Kapoor: Great, can you share your targets and current infra? even ballpark numbers help.
[00:18] James Park: Sure, so p95 we need under 250ms for short prompts (like 32-64 tokens), for longer generation paths p95 can be up to 1.2s. We're also expecting bursts up to 20k concurrent sessions in EU/NA, sustained average concurrency around 6-8k.
[00:33] Ellen Wu: Also streaming is critical, we stream token-by-token to reduce perceived latency. Our UX expects token arrival every ~60-80ms.
[00:40] Alex Chen: Ok, that helps. Are you currently self-hosting or on a managed API?
[00:43] Maria Lopez: We're on a mix — internal models on self-hosted clusters for private data, and we use OpenAI for prototype traffic. Looking to move to a single provider for production to control cost and latency.
[00:55] Priya Kapoor: For the p95 250ms target at 32 tokens, that implies very low generation time per token. With streaming we measure token/sec and tail latency. Typically hosted shared capacity can hit that for smaller models but you need Dedicated for predictable p95 at scale, especially across regions.
[01:12] James Park: Can you clarify the difference operationally? dedicated vs hosted vs private? sometimes the docs gloss over the tradeoffs.
[01:19] Alex Chen: Sure. Hosted is our shared multi-tenant service — low time-to-value, simple API, but noisy neighbors can affect tight SLOs at very high concurrency. Dedicated reserves GPU pools for you with predictable throughput and isolation. Private includes VPC or on-prem where you manage networking and keys — needed for strict compliance or data residency.
[01:38] Maria Lopez: What about token/sec benchmarking — we measured ~12k tokens/sec on our infra for a 13B family model, but that was without KV cache and without your batching optimizations. We need to reach around 50k tokens/sec aggregate for peak traffic.
[01:52] Priya Kapoor: Our Optimize tooling recommends batching and prefix/KV caching; combined those often improve effective tokens/sec by 2-3x for repeat contexts. For a 13B-ish LLM on dedicated A100-like nodes we've seen sustained 30-60k tokens/sec depending on quantization and sequence length.
[02:07] Ellen Wu: How deterministic are those numbers? we worry about p95 tails during peaks.
[02:12] Priya Kapoor: Determinism depends on kernel selection, batching window, and autoscaling. We tune continuous batching windows and have an autoscaler for Dedicated. Our benchmarks include p50/p95/p99 distributions; I'd want to run your actual prompt set through our harness.
[02:24] Alex Chen: Also curious about streaming arrival cadence — you said UX expects token every 60-80ms, that's achievable but depends on pipeline and local latency. For example, network RTT to the region adds to p95. Are your users mostly NA/EU?
[02:38] Maria Lopez: Yes, ~60% NA, 30% EU, small APAC. Latency to NA regions must be excellent.
[02:44] James Park: On security — we need SOC2, SSO (SAML), RBAC, audit logs, and KMS integration. Is Redwood Private required for that or can hosted meet those requirements?
[02:55] Alex Chen: Hosted supports SOC2 and SAML/SSO and KMS integrations for customer-managed keys in some tiers; Dedicated adds network isolation and can be placed in tenant VPCs. Private (VPC/on-prem) is the strongest guarantee for data residency and air-gapped needs. We'll share the security pack.
[03:10] Ellen Wu: Do you support on-prem GPUs or is Private always cloud VPC?
[03:14] Priya Kapoor: We have an on-prem package for regulated customers; it's more involved but possible.
[03:18] Maria Lopez: Back to benchmarks — what do you need from us to run meaningful tests?
[03:21] Priya Kapoor: Sample prompt set, distribution of sequence lengths, concurrency profile (peak and sustained), and a small dataset for any caching checks. We'll spin up a hosted sandbox run first.
[03:31] James Park: We can share a 5000-prompt sample and a traffic histogram. Will that be enough?
[03:35] Priya Kapoor: Yes, that's perfect. We'll run token/sec + tail latency tests with streaming enabled and with/without KV caching and a couple of quant/precision configs.
[03:45] Alex Chen: For the pilot, we'd recommend starting on Hosted sandbox to validate p95 and streaming, then move to Dedicated for predictable capacity. If compliance requires it, we can plan Private on-prem later.
[03:56] Maria Lopez: Pricing — we need a sense of cost per token and dedicated commit sizes.
[03:59] Alex Chen: I'll share a Dedicated sizing + pricing spreadsheet. For Hosted we'll give sample estimates based on your traffic profile.
[04:06] James Park: Any rough numbers for Dedicated sizing to achieve 50k tokens/sec aggregate?
[04:10] Priya Kapoor: Ballpark: for 13B quantized models on A100-style nodes, you'd likely need 3-5 nodes for sustained 50k tokens/sec with good caching; exact depends on sequence length and concurrency. We'll confirm after running your prompts.
[04:22] Ellen Wu: We also want an SLA for p95. Do you commit to p95 targets?
[04:26] Alex Chen: Dedicated plans include latency and uptime SLOs in the contract. We'll propose specific p95 SLOs once we validate benchmarks.
[04:33] Maria Lopez: Great. any blockers from our side?
[04:36] James Park: We'll need a non-prod dataset shared via secure link and credentials for SSO if needed. Also timing: we'd like the POC next week if possible.
[04:45] Priya Kapoor: We can do a POC next week; Priya and Alex will coordinate scheduling.
[04:49] Alex Chen: ok to recap next steps?
[04:51] Maria Lopez: Yes please.
[04:52] Alex Chen: We'll send the pricing & sizing spreadsheet, security pack, and benchmark harness. You'll send the sample prompts and traffic histogram. We'll schedule a 2-hour POC kickoff and run streaming token/sec and p95 tests in our hosted sandbox.
[05:05] Ellen Wu: Sounds good. thanks everyone.
[05:07] Maria Lopez: Thanks.

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mis-hears (e.g., "KV cache" sometimes transcribed as "K-V cash"), speaker overlap a couple of times, timestamps approximate every 15-40s.

References/links mentioned: "Dedicated sizing + pricing spreadsheet (link to be shared)", "security pack (SOC2, KMS, SSO docs)"
